subproblems.title: The Euclidean coefficient norm of n-covectors is a continuous seminorm dominated by the operator norm (reuse of the accepted declaration rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let F := Covector (Euclid P) n (continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm ‖·‖), and let N := covectorEuclideanNorm, i.e. N(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} for the standard orthonormal basis (e_j) of ℝ^P. Then (i) N(α + α') ≤ N(α) + N(α') for all α, α' ∈ F; (ii) N(t·α) = |t|·N(α) for all t ∈ ℝ and α ∈ F; (iii) there is a real C ≥ 0 with N(α) ≤ C·‖α‖ for all α ∈ F; and (iv) N : F → ℝ is continuous. The accepted, reviewed natural-language proof of that node is reproduced verbatim below.

Source: parent proof, step 1 (Properties of N), with all details filled in.

Notation. e_j := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ j (j ∈ Fin P) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P, so ‖e_j‖ = 1. 𝓙 is the finite type of all maps I : Fin n → Fin P, and #𝓙 = Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P). For I ∈ 𝓙, e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), in Lean (fun i => e (I i)). F := Covector (Euclid P) n carries the operator norm ‖·‖ of continuous alternating maps. By definition
N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I∈𝓙} q_I(α)), where q_I(α) := α(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and q_I(α) := 0 otherwise.

1. Coefficient vector. For α ∈ F and I ∈ 𝓙 put c_I(α) := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, and c_I(α) := 0 otherwise. Since (if p then a else 0)² = (if p then a² else 0), q_I(α) = c_I(α)² for every I. Let v(α) ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙 be the vector with coordinates c_I(α); in Lean, v α := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun I => c_I α). The Euclidean norm formula ‖w‖ = √(Σ_I ‖w_I‖²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq), together with ‖w_I‖² = w_I², gives
   N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for every α ∈ F.   (∗)

2. Linearity of v. Evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in the form: (α + α')(e_I) = α(e_I) + α'(e_I) and (t·α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I). So, coordinatewise, c_I(α + α') = c_I(α) + c_I(α') and c_I(t·α) = t·c_I(α); both sides are 0 when I is not strictly increasing. Hence v(α + α') = v(α) + v(α') and v(t·α) = t·v(α) (WithLp.toLp_add, WithLp.toLp_smul).

3. Proof of (i). By (∗), step 2 and the triangle inequality in EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙:
   N(α + α') = ‖v(α) + v(α')‖ ≤ ‖v(α)‖ + ‖v(α')‖ = N(α) + N(α').

4. Proof of (ii). By (∗), step 2 and homogeneity of the norm:
   N(t·α) = ‖t·v(α)‖ = |t|·‖v(α)‖ = |t|·N(α).

5. Coordinate bound. For every I ∈ 𝓙, |c_I(α)| ≤ ‖α‖.
   - If I is strictly increasing, the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖·1 = ‖α‖.
   - Otherwise |c_I(α)| = 0 ≤ ‖α‖.

6. Proof of (iii). Put C := √(#𝓙) ≥ 0. By step 5, c_I(α)² = |c_I(α)|² ≤ ‖α‖² for every I, so Σ_I c_I(α)² ≤ #𝓙·‖α‖². Since √ is monotone and ‖α‖ ≥ 0,
   N(α) = √(Σ_I c_I(α)²) ≤ √(#𝓙·‖α‖²) = √(#𝓙)·√(‖α‖²) = C·‖α‖.

7. Proof of (iv). Let α, α' ∈ F.
   - By (i), N(α) = N((α − α') + α') ≤ N(α − α') + N(α').
   - α' − α = −(α − α') and N(−β) = N(β) (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg, or (ii) with t = −1). So by (i), N(α') = N((α' − α) + α) ≤ N(α' − α) + N(α) = N(α − α') + N(α).
   Together with (iii), |N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C·‖α − α'‖. Thus dist(N(α), N(α')) ≤ C·dist(α, α') for all α, α', so N is Lipschitz with the nonnegative constant C (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul with K := ⟨C, C ≥ 0⟩), hence continuous.

Steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 prove (i)–(iv), with the constant C of (iii) equal to √(Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P)).

v is additive and ℝ-homogeneous, because evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in α.
(i) and (ii) follow from the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the Euclidean norm.

Source: parent proof, elementary fact (E1).
1. (Homogeneity.) Let t ∈ ℝ and α be an n-covector. Then (t•α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I) for every I : Fin n → Fin P, so Σ_I [StrictMono I]((t•α)(e_I))² = t²·S with S := Σ_I [StrictMono I](α(e_I))² ≥ 0. Hence |t•α| = √(t²S) = |t|·√S = |t|·|α|. Also |α| ≥ 0, being a square root, and |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. (r ≥ 0.) By hypothesis 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ r.
3. Put M := T.massOn W and m := M.toReal ≥ 0. Since M ≠ ∞, for every real a, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ M implies a ≤ m (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal).
4. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix ε > 0 and let s := r + ε > 0. Let ω' := s⁻¹ • ω, an element of TestFormOn U n (a submodule) whose underlying form is x ↦ s⁻¹•ω(x). Then tsupport ω' ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, since the tsupport of a scalar multiple is contained in the tsupport. By step 1, |ω'(x)| = s⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ r/s ≤ 1 for all x. Hence ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. Likewise −ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, since it has the same tsupport and |−ω'(x)| = |ω'(x)|.
5. (Bound.) By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ofReal(T ω') ≤ M and ofReal(T(−ω')) ≤ M. By step 3, T ω' ≤ m and −T ω' = T(−ω') ≤ m (T is linear), i.e. |T ω'| ≤ m. By linearity T ω' = s⁻¹·T ω, so |T ω| = s·|T ω'| ≤ (r + ε)·m.
6. (Conclusion.) Since ε > 0 is arbitrary and m ≥ 0, |T ω| ≤ r·m = r·(T.massOn W).toReal.

subproblems.title: A telescoping real series whose remainders tend to zero has sum zero
subproblems.statement: Let a, k : ℕ → ℝ and s ∈ ℝ. Suppose that the real series Σ_j a_j has sum s (HasSum a s, i.e. unconditional summation in ℝ), that a_0 = −k_0 and a_{j+1} = k_j − k_{j+1} for every j ∈ ℕ, and that k_j → 0 as j → ∞. Then s = 0.

Source: the telescoping argument of steps 7 and 8 of the parent's supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, the passage from the limits (19) to the identity (21), chapter-06.txt lines 1792–1820), isolated as a statement about real sequences; the parent uses it once with a_j = W_j(ω) − V_j(ω) − E′_j(ω) − H_j(dω), k_j = K_j(ω) and once with a_j = V_j(dη) − Y_j(η), k_j = L′_j(η).
1. (Partial sums.) For every N ∈ ℕ, Σ_{i=0}^{N} a_i = −k_N. This is proved by induction on N. For N = 0 the sum is a_0 = −k_0 by hypothesis. If Σ_{i=0}^{N} a_i = −k_N, then Σ_{i=0}^{N+1} a_i = Σ_{i=0}^{N} a_i + a_{N+1} = −k_N + (k_N − k_{N+1}) = −k_{N+1} (Finset.sum_range_succ).
2. (Limit from the hypothesis.) Since HasSum a s, the partial sums S_N := Σ_{i<N} a_i tend to s as N → ∞ (HasSum.tendsto_sum_nat). Because N ↦ N + 1 tends to infinity (tendsto_add_atTop_nat 1), the shifted partial sums S_{N+1} = Σ_{i=0}^{N} a_i also tend to s.
3. (Limit from step 1.) By step 1, S_{N+1} = −k_N for every N. Since k_N → 0, −k_N → −0 = 0 (Tendsto.neg). Hence S_{N+1} → 0.
4. (Uniqueness.) Limits of real sequences are unique (ℝ is Hausdorff; tendsto_nhds_unique). Steps 2 and 3 give s = 0. ∎

1. (Evaluation bound.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), r ∈ ℝ with |ω(x)| ≤ r for every x, and j ∈ ℕ with M(X_j) ≠ ∞. Since ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, tsupport ω ⊆ U (the second component of the membership proof, ω.property.2), and M(X_j) = M_U(X_j) by the definition of mass. EB with W := U gives |X_j(ω)| ≤ r·M(X_j).toReal.
2. (Proof of (i).) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and choose c > 0 by CB. Since M(X_j) → 0 and 0 < 1, eventually M(X_j) < 1 < ∞, so eventually M(X_j) ≠ ∞ and, by step 1 with r := c, |X_j(ω)| ≤ c·M(X_j).toReal. The map ENNReal.toReal is continuous at 0 (because 0 ≠ ∞; ENNReal.tendsto_toReal) and 0.toReal = 0, so M(X_j).toReal → 0 and hence c·M(X_j).toReal → c·0 = 0. By the squeeze theorem for norms (squeeze_zero_norm', with ‖X_j(ω)‖ = |X_j(ω)|), X_j(ω) → 0.
3. (Finiteness in (ii).) Assume Σ_j M(X_j) < ∞. Then M(X_j) ≠ ∞ for every j (ENNReal.ne_top_of_tsum_ne_top), the real series Σ_j M(X_j).toReal is summable (ENNReal.summable_toReal), and Σ_j M(X_j).toReal = (Σ_j M(X_j)).toReal (ENNReal.tsum_toReal_eq, all terms finite).

Sibling used: MS = cmc_fc_cs_massOn_sub_le (key mass_sub): M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) for all currents A, B on a common domain and every set G.
Notation. All currents are on univ = ℝ^P and M(X) = M_{ℝ^P}(X). PF1, …, PF5 are the first five conjuncts of (PF) (PF6 is not used). NC_k is the class of X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) with compact support, finite mass and boundaryMassOn X ℝ^P < ∞; PF1–PF4 require their arguments to be NC_k, and PF2–PF5 require all maps involved to be Λ-Lipschitz for one common Λ.
1. (Lipschitz constants.) id is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.id), hence Λ_j-Lipschitz for every j because 1 ≤ Λ_j (LipschitzWith.weaken). φ_j is Λ_j-Lipschitz and Λ_j ≤ Λ_{j+1}, hence also Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz.
2. (Normality of the pieces.) W_j ∈ NC_{m+1}: spt W_j is compact, M(W_j) < ∞, and in degree m + 1 boundaryMassOn W_j ℝ^P is M_{ℝ^P}(∂W_j) = M(∂W_j) < ∞ by definition. D_j, Z_j ∈ NC_m by hypothesis.
3. (Normality of Z_{j+1} − Z_j.) (a) By (S-iii), spt(Z_{j+1} − Z_j) ⊆ spt Z_{j+1} ∪ spt Z_j, which is compact; by (S-ii), spt(Z_{j+1} − Z_j) is closed; a closed subset of a compact set is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). (b) M(Z_{j+1} − Z_j) ≤ M(Z_{j+1}) + M(Z_j) < ∞ by MS (with U = G = ℝ^P). (c) For every n ∈ ℕ and X, Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with boundaryMassOn X ℝ^P < ∞ and boundaryMassOn Y ℝ^P < ∞, also boundaryMassOn (X − Y) ℝ^P < ∞: if n = 0 the value is 0 < ∞ by definition; if n = k + 1, then ∂(X − Y) = ∂X − ∂Y, because both currents take the value X(dη) − Y(dη) at every η ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) (definitions of − and ∂; GeometricCurrentOn.ext), so M(∂(X − Y)) ≤ M(∂X) + M(∂Y) < ∞ by MS. Applying (c) with n = m, X = Z_{j+1}, Y = Z_j shows Z_{j+1} − Z_j ∈ NC_m.
4. (Locality.) PF3 with k := m, Λ := Λ_{j+1}, F := φ_{j+1}, G := id, F' := φ_j, G' := id (all four Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz by step 1), X := Z_j ∈ NC_m, the hypothesis φ_{j+1} = φ_j on spt Z_j and id = id on spt Z_j gives push_m(φ_{j+1}, Z_j) = push_m(φ_j, Z_j) = L′_j and homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, Z_j) = homot_m(φ_j, id, Z_j) = K_j.
5. (Deforming the boundaries.) (a) PF2 with k := m, Λ := Λ_0, F := φ_0, G := id, X := D_0, Y := Z_0 (both NC_m) gives push_m(φ_0, D_0 − Z_0) = Y_0 − L′_0 and homot_m(φ_0, id, D_0 − Z_0) = E′_0 − K_0. (b) Fix j. PF2 with Λ := Λ_{j+1}, F := φ_{j+1}, G := id, X := D_{j+1}, Y := Z_{j+1} − Z_j (NC_m by step 3) gives push_m(φ_{j+1}, D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j)) = Y_{j+1} − push_m(φ_{j+1}, Z_{j+1} − Z_j) and homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j)) = E′_{j+1} − homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, Z_{j+1} − Z_j). PF2 again with X := Z_{j+1}, Y := Z_j gives push_m(φ_{j+1}, Z_{j+1} − Z_j) = L′_{j+1} − push_m(φ_{j+1}, Z_j) and homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, Z_{j+1} − Z_j) = K_{j+1} − homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, Z_j), and by step 4 the last terms are L′_j and K_j. Hence push_m(φ_{j+1}, D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j)) = Y_{j+1} − (L′_{j+1} − L′_j) and homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j)) = E′_{j+1} − (K_{j+1} − K_j).
6. (Homotopy formula; (c1)–(c5).) PF5 with k := m, Λ := Λ_j, F := φ_j, G := id and X := W_j (compact support, M(W_j) < ∞, M(∂W_j) < ∞) gives: (i) ∂V_j = push_m(φ_j, ∂W_j); (ii) push_{m+1}(id, W_j) − V_j − homot_m(φ_j, id, ∂W_j) = ∂H_j; (iii) since W_j is integer multiplicity, V_j and H_j are integer multiplicity, which is (c5). By PF1 (W_j ∈ NC_{m+1}, step 2), push_{m+1}(id, W_j) = W_j, so (ii) reads W_j − V_j − homot_m(φ_j, id, ∂W_j) = ∂H_j. For j = 0, substitute ∂W_0 = D_0 − Z_0 and step 5(a): (ii) becomes (c1) and (i) becomes (c3). For j + 1, substitute ∂W_{j+1} = D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j) and step 5(b): (ii) becomes (c2) and (i) becomes (c4).
7. (Mass bounds; (c6).) PF4 with Λ := Λ_j, F := φ_j, G := id, applied to X := W_j (k = m + 1), X := D_j and X := Z_j (k = m), all NC by step 2, gives M(push_k(φ_j, X)) ≤ Λ_j^k·M(X); and, since dist(φ_j(x), id(x)) = dist(φ_j(x), x) ≤ δ for every x ∈ spt X ⊆ spt W_j ∪ spt D_j ∪ spt Z_j, it gives M(homot_k(φ_j, id, X)) ≤ δ·(2Λ_j)^k·M(X). In [0, ∞], Λ_j ≤ 2Λ_j (as 1 ≤ 2), hence Λ_j^k ≤ (2Λ_j)^k (monotonicity of powers) and Λ_j^k·M(X) ≤ (2Λ_j)^k·M(X); and δ·(2Λ_j)^k·M(X) = δ·((2Λ_j)^k·M(X)) by associativity. These are the six inequalities of (c6).
8. (Supports; (c7).) Let x ∈ spt W_j. Then x ∈ A and dist(φ_j(x), x) ≤ δ, so φ_j(x) ∈ cthickening(δ, A) (Metric.mem_cthickening_of_dist_le), and φ_j(x) ∈ L by hypothesis. By PF4, spt V_j ⊆ φ_j(spt W_j) ⊆ L ∩ cthickening(δ, A). By PF4 also spt H_j ⊆ {φ_j(x) + t(x − φ_j(x)) : x ∈ spt W_j, t ∈ [0, 1]}. For such y = φ_j(x) + t(x − φ_j(x)) we have y − x = (1 − t)(φ_j(x) − x), so dist(y, x) = (1 − t)·dist(φ_j(x), x) ≤ dist(φ_j(x), x) ≤ δ (as 0 ≤ 1 − t ≤ 1); since x ∈ A, y ∈ cthickening(δ, A). Hence spt H_j ⊆ cthickening(δ, A). The same two arguments with D_j in place of W_j, spt D_j ⊆ A' and dist(φ_j(x), x) ≤ δ on spt D_j give spt Y_j ⊆ φ_j(spt D_j) ⊆ cthickening(δ, A') and spt E′_j ⊆ cthickening(δ, A'). ∎

subproblems.statement: Summation of a telescoping series of deformed shells (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, displays (17)–(25)). Assume, as a hypothesis of the statement, (VO): the frozen type of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support (for all P, n, U, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), S(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω is disjoint from spt S). Let P, m ∈ ℕ and assume (S-i): for every closed E ⊆ ℝ^P and every X ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) (domain univ) such that X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) whose tsupport is disjoint from E, spt X ⊆ E (conjunct (i), in degree m, of the frozen type of Submission.cmcsd_support_calculus, taken as a hypothesis); assume also (IMS), the conclusion of the frozen type of Submission.cmcdt_im_series for this P (taken verbatim as a hypothesis): for every k ∈ ℕ and all W_i ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) (i ∈ ℕ, domain univ) with Σ_i M(W_i) < ∞ (tsum in [0, ∞]) there is S ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) such that: for every test form ω, the series Σ_i W_i(ω) has sum S(ω) (HasSum); M(S) ≤ Σ_i M(W_i); spt S ⊆ closure(⋃_i spt W_i); and if every W_i is integer multiplicity then S is integer multiplicity. Let T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P), and for j ∈ ℕ let W_j, V_j, E′_j, K_j ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P), H_j ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P), Y_j, L′_j ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) (all on univ); let a, b, c : ℕ → [0, ∞], δ ∈ ℝ and K₁, K₂, K₃ ⊆ ℝ^P. Assume: Σ_j W_j(ω) = T(ω) (HasSum) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P); (I1) W_0 − V_0 − (E′_0 − K_0) = ∂H_0; (I2) W_{j+1} − V_{j+1} − (E′_{j+1} − (K_{j+1} − K_j)) = ∂H_{j+1} for all j; (I3) ∂V_0 = Y_0 − L′_0; (I4) ∂V_{j+1} = Y_{j+1} − (L′_{j+1} − L′_j) for all j; V_j and H_j are integer multiplicity for all j; for all j, M(V_j) ≤ a_j, M(H_j) ≤ δ·a_j, M(Y_j) ≤ b_j, M(E′_j) ≤ δ·b_j, M(L′_j) ≤ c_j and M(K_j) ≤ δ·c_j (δ read as ENNReal.ofReal δ); Σ_j a_j < ∞, Σ_j b_j < ∞ and c_j → 0 in [0, ∞]; K₁, K₂, K₃ are closed; for all j, spt V_j ⊆ K₁, spt H_j ⊆ K₂, spt Y_j ⊆ K₃ and spt E′_j ⊆ K₃. Then there are Q₀ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P), R₁ ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) and S₁ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with: Q₀ and R₁ integer multiplicity; T − Q₀ − S₁ = ∂R₁; spt Q₀ ⊆ K₁, spt R₁ ⊆ K₂, spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ K₃, spt S₁ ⊆ K₃; M(Q₀) ≤ Σ_j a_j, M(∂Q₀) ≤ Σ_j b_j, M(R₁) ≤ δ·Σ_j a_j and M(S₁) ≤ δ·Σ_j b_j. Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)); for U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^k(U) = TestFormOn U k (smooth k-forms on ℝ^P whose compact tsupport lies in U) and 𝒟_k(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U k (SimonGMT Chapter06), X(ω) the value of X on ω; X − Y is the contract subtraction, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) (definitional); ∂X = X.boundary, ∂X(η) = X(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, dη = exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k η, whose underlying form is exteriorDerivative η); currents are equal when their values agree (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector. M_G(X) = X.massOn G ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (such ω are admissible for M_G, massAdmissibleOn U k G); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X); boundaryMassOn X G = M_G(∂X) if k ≥ 1 and 0 if k = 0. spt X = X.support (Simon 6.2.11) = U minus the zero region, the union of the open W with compact closure contained in U on which X vanishes (X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W). IM = IsIntegerMultiplicity: X is represented by an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) of the contract, i.e. X(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ. Metric.cthickening δ E = {x : infEdist x E ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ}; in a mass bound, a real factor δ is read as ENNReal.ofReal δ.

Source: steps 5–9 of the parent's supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1: summation of the deformed pieces (17)–(19), the identity (20)–(21), and the support and mass statements (22)–(25), chapter-06.txt lines 1775–1838), with the deformed pieces V_j = push(φ_j, W_j), H_j, Y_j, E′_j, L′_j, K_j of the parent replaced by abstract sequences satisfying the identities the parent derives for them. Siblings used: TEL = cmcsdtd_hasSum_telescoping_eq_zero (key telescoping_real); ME = cmcsdtd_mass_controls_eval (key mass_eval), applied with U := ℝ^P in degrees m and m + 1. Throughout, δ in a mass bound means ENNReal.ofReal δ, which is < ∞; for a test form ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P), dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k ω, so that ∂X(ω) = X(dω) and (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) hold definitionally.
1. (Mass series.) Termwise comparison (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum) and pulling out the constant (ENNReal.tsum_mul_left) give Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ Σ_j a_j, Σ_j M(H_j) ≤ Σ_j δ·a_j = δ·Σ_j a_j, Σ_j M(Y_j) ≤ Σ_j b_j and Σ_j M(E′_j) ≤ δ·Σ_j b_j. All four are finite, because Σ a_j, Σ b_j < ∞ and δ < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top).
2. (Remainders.) 0 ≤ M(L′_j) ≤ c_j with c_j → 0, and 0 ≤ M(K_j) ≤ δ·c_j with δ·c_j → δ·0 = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, using δ ≠ ∞). By the squeeze theorem in [0, ∞] (tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le), M(L′_j) → 0 and M(K_j) → 0.
3. (The three limits.) IMS with k := m and the sequence (V_j) (finite mass series by step 1) gives Q₀ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with HasSum (V_j(ω))_j (Q₀(ω)) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P), M(Q₀) ≤ Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ Σ_j a_j, spt Q₀ ⊆ closure ⋃_j spt V_j ⊆ K₁ (⋃_j spt V_j ⊆ K₁ and K₁ is closed; closure_minimal), and Q₀ integer multiplicity because every V_j is. IMS with k := m + 1 and (H_j) (degree (m + 1) + 1 = m + 2) gives R₁ ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) with HasSum (H_j(ζ))_j (R₁(ζ)) for every ζ ∈ 𝒟^{m+2}(ℝ^P), M(R₁) ≤ Σ_j M(H_j) ≤ δ·Σ_j a_j, spt R₁ ⊆ K₂, and R₁ integer multiplicity. IMS with k := m and (E′_j) gives S₁ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with HasSum (E′_j(ω))_j (S₁(ω)), M(S₁) ≤ δ·Σ_j b_j and spt S₁ ⊆ K₃.
4. (T − Q₀ − S₁ = ∂R₁.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) and put α_j := W_j(ω) − V_j(ω) − E′_j(ω) − H_j(dω). From the hypothesis HasSum (W_j(ω)) (T(ω)) and step 3 (with ζ := dω), HasSum (α_j)_j (T(ω) − Q₀(ω) − S₁(ω) − R₁(dω)) (HasSum.sub three times). Evaluating (I1) at ω gives W_0(ω) − V_0(ω) − (E′_0(ω) − K_0(ω)) = H_0(dω), i.e. α_0 = −K_0(ω); evaluating (I2) at ω gives W_{j+1}(ω) − V_{j+1}(ω) − (E′_{j+1}(ω) − (K_{j+1}(ω) − K_j(ω))) = H_{j+1}(dω), i.e. α_{j+1} = K_j(ω) − K_{j+1}(ω). By step 2 and ME (i) (degree m + 1), K_j(ω) → 0. TEL with a := α and k := (K_j(ω))_j gives T(ω) − Q₀(ω) − S₁(ω) − R₁(dω) = 0, i.e. (T − Q₀ − S₁)(ω) = R₁(dω) = ∂R₁(ω). As ω is arbitrary, T − Q₀ − S₁ = ∂R₁ (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
5. (∂Q₀ is the weak sum of the Y_j.) Fix η ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P). By step 1 and ME (ii)(a) (degree m), the series Σ_j Y_j(η) is summable; let y := Σ_j Y_j(η), so HasSum (Y_j(η))_j y. By step 3 with ω := dη, HasSum (V_j(dη))_j (Q₀(dη)); hence β_j := V_j(dη) − Y_j(η) satisfies HasSum (β_j)_j (Q₀(dη) − y) (HasSum.sub). Evaluating (I3) and (I4) at η gives V_0(dη) = Y_0(η) − L′_0(η) and V_{j+1}(dη) = Y_{j+1}(η) − (L′_{j+1}(η) − L′_j(η)), i.e. β_0 = −L′_0(η) and β_{j+1} = L′_j(η) − L′_{j+1}(η). By step 2 and ME (i) (degree m), L′_j(η) → 0. TEL gives Q₀(dη) − y = 0. Hence ∂Q₀(η) = Q₀(dη) = y, and HasSum (Y_j(η))_j (∂Q₀(η)).
6. (Mass of ∂Q₀.) By step 5 and ME (ii)(b) (degree m, with X_j := Y_j, Y := ∂Q₀, and Σ_j M(Y_j) < ∞ by step 1), M(∂Q₀) ≤ Σ_j M(Y_j) ≤ Σ_j b_j.
7. (Support of ∂Q₀.) Let η ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport η disjoint from K₃. For every j, spt Y_j ⊆ K₃, so tsupport η is disjoint from spt Y_j and (VO) gives Y_j(η) = 0. By step 5 the series of zeros has sum ∂Q₀(η), so ∂Q₀(η) = 0 (uniqueness of sums: HasSum.unique with hasSum_zero). By (S-i) with E := K₃ (closed) and X := ∂Q₀, spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ K₃.
8. (Conclusion.) Q₀, R₁, S₁ satisfy: Q₀ and R₁ are integer multiplicity (step 3); T − Q₀ − S₁ = ∂R₁ (step 4); spt Q₀ ⊆ K₁, spt R₁ ⊆ K₂ and spt S₁ ⊆ K₃ (step 3), spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ K₃ (step 7); M(Q₀) ≤ Σ_j a_j, M(R₁) ≤ δ·Σ_j a_j and M(S₁) ≤ δ·Σ_j b_j (step 3), M(∂Q₀) ≤ Σ_j b_j (step 6). ∎
